Subject: Performance SLO qualification: latency & throughput follow-up

Hi Aisha / Samir —

Thanks again for the call today — great overview of the Nova Retail chat assistant use case. Per our conversation, I wanted to summarize the key SLOs and the open items so we can scope a pilot and a quick cost/throughput estimate.

Recap of targets you mentioned (please correct if I misheard):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end streaming response <= 200ms (target); p50 <= 80ms
- Throughput: sustain burst up to 250 QPS for single-region traffic; typical steady-state ~60 QPS
- Concurrency: ~200 concurrent active users during peak events
- Streaming: partial-token streaming is required (clients render token-by-token) — can't buffer full responses
- Response size: avg. ~120 tokens per response; 95th percentile ~600 tokens
- Quality: low hallucination on product/inventory facts (we discussed using context grounding + retrieval)

Attachments: I attached an SLO worksheet (nova_slo_requirements.xlsx) — please fill in any missing numeric distributions (e.g., arrival pattern, token distributions by endpoint).

Next steps (proposed):
1) You confirm the arrival profile and token distribution in the worksheet (Aisha) — this will influence batching/caching configs.
2) Our infra engineering (Dylan) will propose 2 config options: Hosted (fast to run) and Dedicated (predictable throughput). Expect a short write-up with expected p95/p50 latency and rough monthly estimate.
3) Schedule a ~30m technical kickoff next week with your infra/ML folks to align on streaming implementation and retrieval integration.

Technical notes for the team: potential levers we'll evaluate to hit the SLOs while controlling cost — continuous batching + smallish batch windows for streaming, prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, int8/int4 quantization profiles for cheaper model variants, and model variants tradeoffs (13b vs 70b). We'll include rough estimates for each.

Thanks — I'll loop in the engineer once we get the completed worksheet.

Best,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this is accurate. A few clarifications from our side after today's sync:

- Streaming behavior: our UI expects progressive tokens and will call the endpoint with a keep-alive. We measure rendering latency as time from token emitted by the model to first render. Our internal goal is first-token render < 200ms during normal traffic (we can tolerate slightly higher in extreme bursts), and per-token pacing should be < 80ms on average.
- Traffic pattern: steady sessions are relatively chatty — typical user generates ~6 requests per session. Peak traffic comes from promotional events (flash sales) where concurrency spikes and many users request the same product prompts (so caching might help).
- Token distribution: average response ~120 tokens; heavy-detail responses ~400–600 tokens (rare).
- Security/compliance: we need assurance that customer data used for retrieval won't be cached or leaked across tenants (we can share an initial security checklist if needed).
- Cost question: ballpark cost sensitivity — we're evaluating vendor options and would like a 1M-token monthly cost comparison for your recommended config.

I've attached a filled-first-pass of the worksheet (novaretail_slo_completed.xlsx) — it's minimal but should help.

Aisha

Hi Aisha — thanks for the worksheet and the clarifications. I've sketched two candidate configs and the expected tradeoffs below. These are rough engineering estimates; we'll run a small benchmark during the pilot to validate.

Config A — Hosted (fastest to pilot)\- Model: 13B open model variant, quantized to q4f16 for inference accuracy/cost balance\- Inference mode: streaming with 8-token micro-chunk flush (continuous batching enabled)\- Batching: adaptive continuous batching targeting 20–40ms batching window to preserve streaming latency\- Caching: prefix/KV cache for top 25% of repeated prompts (estimated hit rate 20–30% during promos)\- Expected p50/p95 (end-to-end streaming emit): ~60ms / ~140ms for average response (120 tokens); heavy responses p95 may exceed target for 600-token replies unless we increase concurrency/instances\- Concurrency & throughput: single pool (4 x A100-class GPUs equiv) can sustain ~150–220 concurrent streaming sessions depending on token churn\- Cost: lowest incremental compute cost; approximate comparison: ~ $X per 1M tokens (we'll provide a precise quote).

Config B — Dedicated (predictable SLO)\- Model: 13B or 30B quantized (q8/q4 options) pinned to dedicated GPU pool\- Inference mode: streaming, continuous batching with lower variance (reserved slots)\- Autoscaling: configured for steady 60 QPS with burst to 250 QPS; configured canary fallbacks to smaller model variant under pressure\- Expected p50/p95: ~50ms / ~120ms (more stable at p95 because of reserved capacity)\- Concurrency: designed for the 200 concurrent user target with headroom\- Cost: higher fixed cost (reserved capacity) but predictable monthly spend and SLO commitments

Cost/performance levers (how we'll hit the SLOs):
1) Continuous batching: keeps latency low by grouping small windows and maintaining streaming constraints. We'll tune batch windows per endpoint.
2) Prefix/KV caching: for repeated product prompts, caching cut compute by ~20–40% in similar customers — big win during promo spikes.
3) Quantization profiles: q4 reduces memory and improves throughput; quality tradeoff is model-dependent. We'll run A/B on fidelity vs cost.
4) Model variants + routing: route by policy (latency-sensitive vs cost-sensitive routes). We can fallback to a smaller variant during extreme bursts.
5) Chunked streaming size: reducing micro-chunk size reduces perceived latency but increases compute overhead; we'll find a sweet spot (~6–12 tokens/chunk).

Suggested pilot plan:
- 2-week technical benchmark with your sample traffic (we'll provide a small harness)
- Run comparisons: (i) hosted q4 13B with caching, (ii) dedicated q8 13B pinned, and (iii) small fallback 7B variant for extreme bursts
- Provide concrete p50/p95, cost/M-token, and recommended production config

Attached: redwood-performance-profiles.pdf (high-level perf numbers and quantization notes). I'll follow up with a short benchmark script and an expected timeline (3–5 business days to get initial numbers once we have sample traffic).

Let me know if you'd like us to include tokenization breakouts or to test with your retrieval stack enabled.

Thanks,
